items.hook: War and Peace in the Global Village is a 1968 book by Marshall McLuhan and Quentin Fiore.
items.body: It contains a collage of images and text that illustrates the effects of electronic media and new technology on man. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Pierre Clementi, real name Francis Anthony Clementi, was a French politician active during the 1930s and the occupation of France during the Second World War.
items.body: He was the founder and leader of the French National-Collectivist Party, which espoused a platform of National Communism, a combination of Fascism, French nationalism and to a certain extent Communism. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Towelhead is a novel written by American novelist Alicia Erian and first published April 6, 2005.
items.body: Alicia Erian is the first holder of the Newhouse Visiting Professorship of Creative Writing at Wellesley College in Massachusetts. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Tiger Rising is a 2022 American drama film written and directed by Ray Giarratana and starring Christian Convery, Madalen Mills, Katharine McPhee, Sam Trammell, Dennis Quaid and Queen Latifah.
items.body: It is based on the 2001 book of the same name by Kate DiCamillo. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Songs created by AI banned from Australia's music charts
items.body: The move comes weeks after a DJ admitted using AI to remix a Madonna song that topped the Australian charts.

items.hook: The Remains of the Day is a 1993 drama film adapted from the Booker Prize–winning 1989 novel by Kazuo Ishiguro.
items.body: The film was directed by James Ivory, produced by Ismail Merchant, Mike Nichols, and John Calley and adapted by Ruth Prawer Jhabvala. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, essayist, poet and travel writer.
items.body: He is best known for the novels Treasure Island (1883), Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886), and Kidnapped (1886) and for the poetry collection A Child's Garden of Verses (1885). One of those things you can't un-know.
